title: Per-model & per-route retention overrides with verifiable evidence handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a flexible retention override layer that allows operators and customers to set retention windows at model and route granularity (prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics). Expose an evidence handoff mechanism that packages kept data with a verifiable manifest for audits and legal requests.

Goals:
- Allow per-model and per-route TTL configuration that overrides global defaults for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Ensure retention settings are enforced in the ingestion path and at rest (S3/Blob + index metadata).
- Provide an automated evidence export endpoint and CLI that bundles time-bounded artifacts (prompt/response blobs, request logs, metrics snapshots) with checksums and a signed manifest for auditors.
- Minimize latency impact on the runtime; prefer asynchronous eviction and archival where possible.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API: Admin API accepts retention overrides at model and route levels and surfaces effective TTL for any given request (global -> model -> route precedence).
2) Enforcement: Requests older than their effective TTL are excluded from queryable stores and telemetry dashboards within 15 minutes of expiry in hosted mode, and documented asynchronous behavior for Dedicated/Private.
3) Evidence export: Given a time window and a tenant/model/route selector, the system produces a bundle with: data files (ndjson), metrics CSV, access logs, and a manifest.json containing SHA256 checksums and a signed hash.
4) Auditability: All retention changes recorded in audit log (who, when, from where) and visible in Console UI with diff view.
5) E2E tests and regression checks in CI; quality gates blocking release if manifest verification or TTL enforcement regress.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Enforcement path: Two-phase approach: (1) soft-filtering at query and streaming edges to fast-return and avoid serving expired data, (2) background eviction/archival pipeline to reclaim storage. This reduces p99 latency risk but admits a small window where expired data could still be present in cold storage before eviction.
- Per-route overrides cause cardinality concerns in index metadata; we store only hashed selectors in route_index to keep metadata small and use bloom filters for quick matching.
- Evidence bundle size: For large tenants, exports can be multi-GB. We provide an async job with pre-signed download links and optional streamed tarball for smaller exports.
- Security: Signed manifest requires KMS integration for signing; private deployments may use customer-provided HSM. This is gated behind security review.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind "per_route_retention" for 1% of hosted tenants + internal Redwood tenants.
2) Canary in Dedicated with a single customer pilot.
3) Private deployment: release package and runbook, require an on-site security review.

Open questions:
- Should we expose per-tenant default retention templates in the Console or restrict to API-only at first? PM leaning toward Console templates for enterprise UX.
- SLA for evidence export turnaround for very large bundles ( > 50GB ).

Notes on observability/telemetry:
- Add TTL enforcement metric (ttl.expired_processed_count) and lag gauge (ttl.eviction_lag_seconds).
- Add signal to Optimize recommendations to avoid recommending quantization/batching settings that conflict with archival window assumptions.
